wake.nameText: What do you want to say to call K-Desktop? It learns from your voice, so it can be a made-up word such as “KDesktop”.
wake.nameTips: Best with 2 to 4 syllables and not something you say in normal conversation. You can add several, each with its own recording.
wake.silenceText: Stay quiet for 3 seconds so I can measure the background noise where you are.
wake.noise.medium: Medium background noise ({0}). Should be fine.
wake.noise.high: Quite a lot of background noise ({0}): the word will be recognised less well. If you can, turn the music off or move the mic away from the fan.

wake.issue.NoSpeech: I didn’t hear you. Press to continue and say it again.
wake.issue.TooShort: Too short. Press to continue and repeat it.
wake.issue.TooLong: Too long (over 2.5 s). Press to continue and repeat it.
wake.issue.TooQuiet: Very quiet: move closer to the mic or speak louder.
wake.issue.Clipped: Clipped: move a little away from the mic or lower its volume.
wake.issue.Odd: Very different from the others. Press to continue and repeat it.
wake.speechText: Now talk normally for about 10 seconds WITHOUT saying “{0}”: read the text below or tell what you did today. This way your normal speech won’t set it off by mistake.
wake.speechSample: “This morning I checked my email, tidied a few folders on the desktop and then put on some music while I was cooking.”

wake.speechDone: Done: the closest thing you said reached {0}; the threshold is {1}.
wake.testText: Say “{0}” (and, if you like, an order after it: “{0}, open the browser”) to see whether it is recognised. Try as many times as you like.
wake.needModels: Download the voice models first (above, in this same section).

event.enabledHint: On: K-Desktop watches for what sets it off
event.emptyText: An event runs commands on its own when something happens: a program opens, a time of day, a while without using the PC, locking it…
event.suspended: Stopped for a few minutes: it fired too many times in a row (a loop?)
event.testHint: Runs its commands now, without checking «Only if» or the pause
event.newCommandHint: Creates a hidden command for this event and opens it so you can add its actions.
event.noCommands: It doesn't run anything yet: add one or more commands.
event.exitNote: On exit they all run at once, 5 s at most, so exiting never hangs.
event.endHint.ProcessStart: When the program closes (with several windows or processes, when the last one closes).
event.endHint.Foreground: When it stops being in front.
event.endHint.Idle: When you use the PC again.
event.endHint.AudioDevice: When it is disconnected, or stops being the default output.
event.endHint.Network: When it disconnects from that network (or there is network again).
event.conditionsNone: No conditions: it always fires. Add the ones you want (the same as «If…»: schedule, a program open, the network, the battery…).
event.conditionTest: Test whether it is met now
event.createCommand: Create a command that runs it
event.cooldownHint: If it fires again sooner, it does nothing. 0 = always. Also, an event that fires more than 10 times in a minute stops for 10 minutes.
event.deleteText: Delete “{0}”? Its commands are not deleted.
event.runIfMissed: If it was missed, run it on start
event.runIfMissedHint: If K-Desktop was closed or the PC asleep at that time, it runs as soon as it can (once, the last one missed).
event.dateHint: With a day, only that day. Without one, it repeats.
event.onceHint: It is deleted after it runs.
event.askNone: You can ask an assistant for something, as if you said it.
event.askTextHint: Check the weather and send it to me on Telegram
event.askHint: It asks after the commands, as if you said it. If the assistant is not on the desktop, nothing happens.
event.scheduledApproved: When you asked, you approved it doing without asking: {0}. Anything else that would ask, it won't do.
event.scheduledNothing: You approved nothing that asks: it will only do what needs no permission.
event.includeRunning: Also if it was already open when K-Desktop started
event.hint.appStart: Runs every time K-Desktop starts, its commands one after another and the events in the order of the list (drag to change it). Not after an update, nor while paused.
event.hint.appExit: Runs when K-Desktop exits, when the Windows session ends or when shutting down with the Power action. Not when it restarts to update itself.
event.hint.interval: It counts from when K-Desktop starts (or from when you change the event).
event.hint.processStart: Checked every 2 seconds. With several programs, it starts when the first opens and ends when the last closes.
event.hint.foreground: When one of these programs comes to the front (with a short margin so a quick Alt+Tab doesn't count).
event.hint.idle: No keyboard or mouse in that time. What macros, K-Board or the web app touchpad type or move also counts as using the PC.
event.hint.session: When going to sleep Windows leaves very little time: use quick commands (mute, pause the music…).
enum.session.Suspend: When the PC goes to sleep
event.kind.AppStart.desc: What used to be «Run on startup» in each command.
event.kind.AppExit.desc: What used to be «Run on exit» in each command.
event.kind.Time.desc: Every day or only on some days of the week, at the time you say.
event.kind.Interval.desc: Every N minutes while K-Desktop is running.
event.kind.ProcessStart.desc: When it opens (and, in «When it ends», when it closes). For example: when Steam opens, audio output to the headphones.
event.kind.Foreground.desc: When its window comes to the front (and, in «When it ends», when it stops being there).
event.kind.Idle.desc: After some minutes without touching the keyboard or mouse (and, in «When it ends», when you come back).
event.kind.Session.desc: When the session is locked or unlocked, or the PC goes to sleep or wakes up.
event.kind.PowerSource.desc: When a laptop goes on battery or back on mains power.
event.kind.File.desc: When a file in a folder appears, changes, is deleted or is renamed. For example, a new image in the ComfyUI output folder.
event.kind.RemoteCall.desc: When another computer, Home Assistant or a script asks for it by name, over UDP or the web.
event.summary.remoteCallOwn: When a call with its name arrives
event.hint.remoteCall: Case and accents don’t matter. Over UDP it needs «Remote control» on with «Events» allowed (and the key, if there is one, from another computer); over the web, another computer needs the token of a paired device.
event.hint.remoteCallExamples:
UDP:  event door
HTTP: POST http://<PC>:2502/api/event
      X-KD: 1
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
      {"name": "door"}
event.kind.Device.desc: When a USB stick, disk or card is connected (and, in «When it ends», when it is removed).
event.kind.Network.desc: When connecting to a network (or any) or when left without network; «When it ends», when that changes back.
event.kind.Gadget.desc: When a controller (Bluetooth or USB), a keyboard, a headset, a USB gadget… is connected; «When it ends», when it is disconnected. For example: when the controller is turned on, open Steam Big Picture.
event.endHint.Gadget: When it is disconnected (with a name, when the last thing with that name goes).
event.endHint.Load: When it stops holding for the same time (back to normal).
event.endHint.Battery: When the battery is back on the other side of the limit.
event.endHint.Display: When that screen is taken out.
event.hint.gadget: Names are the Device Manager’s; the list includes paired Bluetooth devices even when they are off. Part of the name is enough («8bitdo», «xbox»). A Bluetooth device counts only while connected; it may take up to 15 s to be noticed.
event.kind.Load.desc: When the CPU, the graphics card, the memory or the VRAM goes above a % (or below it) for a while: a game or a render starts, a download finishes… «When it ends», when it's back to normal.
event.kind.Battery.desc: When the battery goes below a % (or above it). «When it ends», when it is back on the other side.
event.kind.Sun.desc: At sunrise or sunset where you are, or some minutes before or after. For example, switching Windows to dark at sunset.
event.kind.Display.desc: When you plug in or take out a monitor or the TV. For example, changing the projection or the audio output when the TV is connected.
event.hint.load: It's measured every 2 s, as in Task Manager (GPU = its 3D engine). Examples: GPU above 50 % for 30 s → High performance plan, and «When it ends» → Balanced; CPU below 10 % for 600 s → shut down when a render finishes.
event.kind.AudioDevice.desc: When headphones, a speaker or a microphone (USB, Bluetooth…) are connected, or one becomes the default; «When it ends», when it is disconnected or stops being it.
event.summary.audioDefaultAnyInput: When the default audio input changes
event.summary.audioAny: When an audio device is connected
event.summary.audioDefaultAny: When the default audio output changes
event.hint.audio: Output devices (those in Windows Sound). The name can be a part: «JBL», «Headphones».
event.hint.audioInput: Input devices (microphones, those in Windows Sound). The name can be a part: «Yeti», «Headset».
event.hint.network: The name is the one Windows gives the network: the Wi-Fi’s, or «Network 2» for a cable. The list shows the ones connected now.
event.hint.drive: A letter only matches that letter; a name is looked for in the drive’s label (the one shown in Explorer).
event.hint.file: Filter with wildcards: *.png, render_*.mp4… (* = any). A new or changed file waits until it stops growing for a second; each time fires the event once. The commands get its path in {file}.
event.hint.battery: It fires when it crosses the limit (not if it is already below when watching starts). On a PC without a battery it does nothing.
event.sunPlaceHint: Where you are (assistant options or Windows)
event.sunTodayIs: Today in {0}: sunrise at {1}, sunset at {2}
event.sunNotFound: The place can't be found: write your town (or allow location in Windows).
event.hint.sun: The time is worked out on the PC for each day. Empty: «Where you are» in the assistant options or, without it, Windows' location. If the PC is asleep at that time, it does not fire that day.
event.hint.display: A TV plugged in but not in use yet counts too (to change the projection when it is connected). «When it ends», when it is taken out. The commands get its name in {screen}.
event.summary.power.Mains: When it goes back on mains
enum.powerSource.Mains: When it goes back on mains
event.hint.power: Only on computers with a battery (or a UPS that tells Windows).

assistant.prompt.who: Your name is {0} and you live on the user's Windows desktop, inside K-Desktop.
assistant.prompt.style: Once you have done what they ask (with whatever tools it takes), your final answer is always in English, in one or two short sentences, with no lists, no Markdown and no emojis: what you say appears in a speech bubble. Write numbers and times with digits. The user is an adult: do what they ask (open any website or program) without judging or lecturing. Don't end with a question unless you need something to do what they ask. If a tool gives you something long (a list of names or things), do not read it all: say how many there are and three at most, unless they ask for all of them.
assistant.prompt.tools: Use a tool when the user asks you to do something or to know something it knows (the time, their notes, their timers, a calculation): don't guess. Chatting, giving an opinion or telling something needs no tool: answer yourself. Never say you did something no tool did in this answer. If no tool does what they ask, say so simply: don't use one that does something else (opening is not closing). Their K-Desktop commands run with run_command; if they ask what a command does or which commands they have, look it up with describe_command or find_command: don't make up what they do. Never name your tools to the user.

assistant.memory.learn:
You read an exchange between a user and their assistant. Extract ONLY new, lasting facts about the user worth remembering for months: their name, family, pets, work or studies, likes and hobbies, health, important dates and plans. Only take what the user says about themselves, never what the assistant says.
Don't include greetings, passing moods, questions, one-off requests or anything about the assistant (nor complaints, anger or opinions about it or about what it can or can't do). Nothing that comes from what is read on the screen or on a web page, nor about K-Desktop or the programs they use. Don't repeat what is already known.
Write each fact in English, as a short sentence in the third person ("Their name is Mark", "They love coffee").
Reply ONLY with JSON: {"memories":[{"text":"...","kind":"fact|like|event","importance":0.0-1.0}]}
If there is nothing new, reply {"memories":[]}.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.intro: K-Desktop does for you what you repeat every day: open programs, type texts, move windows, control the music… with a hotkey, a menu or your voice. Start by choosing how you want it to look.
welcome.whatText: It all revolves around commands: you decide what they do and how they start.
welcome.featCommandsText: One or more actions started with a keyboard or mouse hotkey.
welcome.featMenusText: Menus with your commands that appear where the mouse is.
welcome.featLauncherText: A search box to open commands, programs and websites.
welcome.featVoiceText: Say what you want to do and K-Desktop does it. Works offline.
welcome.featKBoardText: Changes what the keys and mouse buttons do.
welcome.featAssistantsText: Characters on your desktop you can talk to, with AI on your PC.
welcome.basicsText: A few settings to start with. You can change everything later in Settings.
welcome.startupHint: K-Desktop opens by itself when the PC starts, so your hotkeys always work.
welcome.launcherKeyHint: Opens the search box from anywhere.
welcome.trayTip: K-Desktop keeps working when you close the window: it is in the icon next to the clock. Click it to come back.
welcome.voiceText: Optional. Your voice is understood on your PC, nothing is sent to the internet. The voice models are downloaded once.
welcome.voiceMissing: The voice models still have to be downloaded ({0}). You can go on while they download.
welcome.voiceKeyHint: Hold it down while you say the order.
welcome.voiceLater: Later, in Settings → Wake words, you can record a word to call K-Desktop without touching anything.
welcome.assistantsText: Optional. Assistants are characters that live on your desktop: you talk or write to them and they do things for you, like your commands, with gestures you can see.
welcome.assistantsOnHint: Off, K-Desktop loads nothing of them.
welcome.assistantsBrain: They are installed from Settings → Catalog and, to chat, they need an AI model (Settings → Brain).
welcome.doneText: You can start using K-Desktop. To begin, create your first command in Commands: give it a name, add an action and choose a hotkey.
welcome.again: You can see this welcome again in About.

arrangement.infoCut: In the drawing, a click marks a zone and another click on it splits it in two (with Shift, horizontally). Drag the lines to resize (they snap to ½, ⅓ and ¼) and press a line's ✕ to join its two zones.
arrangement.infoPrograms: Each zone has its programs: when it is put, their windows go there (several of the same program, by title and otherwise in order). A pinned program goes back to the exact place it had when saved.
arrangement.infoUse: It is put with «Test», with a command's «Window layout» action or from an event (e.g. «Screen plugged in or out»). The last one put on each monitor is the one Shift + drag and Win + Alt + ← / → use.
macro.infoRecord: «Record» starts after a 3-second countdown and keeps your keys and mouse with their timing.
macro.infoSteps: Drag the steps to move them; pick several with Ctrl or Shift, and Delete removes them. Each step has its pause before it, in milliseconds.
macro.infoKeys: Ctrl + Z undoes and Ctrl + Y redoes the changes to the steps.

accounts.title: Connected accounts
accounts.intro: Google and Microsoft accounts for the calendar and mail. You sign in in your browser: K-Desktop never sees your password, and keeps the permission encrypted only for this user on this PC.
accounts.use.mailLong: Mail (read, notify, drafts and send with confirmation)
accounts.disconnectGoogle: Disconnect {0}? The permission is revoked at Google and K-Desktop stops using its calendars and mail. Nothing is deleted from your account.
accounts.disconnectMicrosoft: Disconnect {0}? K-Desktop forgets the permission and stops using its calendars and mail. Microsoft doesn’t let a program revoke it: if you want, also remove it at account.microsoft.com › Privacy › Apps and services.
accounts.connectIntro: Your browser opens to sign in and give permission. You can connect an account again to grant it more permissions (for example, mail).
accounts.waiting: Waiting for you to sign in in the browser… (5 minutes at most)
accounts.chooseUse: Choose what the account is for (calendar, mail or both).
accounts.googleNeedsApp: To connect Google you need your own Client ID (below, with the guide).
accounts.microsoftNeedsApp: To connect Microsoft, enter your application’s ID below (with the guide).
accounts.alternative: Don’t want to create an application? You can see Google and Outlook read-only with their secret .ics address (Options › Calendars › Subscriptions), and connect mail with an app password.
accounts.appsIntro: Which application accounts connect with. Google requires verifying applications that read the calendar or mail, so yours is used: it’s free and for your own use it doesn’t need verifying.
accounts.googleGuide: At console.cloud.google.com: create a project and enable “Google Calendar API”. In “OAuth consent screen” choose “External” and publish it “In production” (unverified is fine for you; you’ll see the “unverified app” warning. In “Testing” the permission expires after 7 days). In “Credentials” create an “OAuth client ID” of type “Desktop app” and copy its ID and secret here. Gmail goes through IMAP: no other API is needed.
accounts.microsoftGuide: At entra.microsoft.com › App registrations › New registration: “Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts”. In “Authentication” add the “Mobile and desktop applications” platform with http://localhost and turn on “Allow public client flows”. Copy the “Application (client) ID” here.
